assessment: Payne et al. present a novel model that predicts sites and directions of plasticity within the vestibular cerebellum to explain the basis for learned adjustments to reflexive eye movements in monkeys. The model is convincingly constrained by prior biological observations and makes an important prediction about the level of feedback available to the cerebellar cortex and how this level determines the plasticity required to explain post-learning changes in activity. Overall, a number of exciting and testable experiments will likely be motivated by this study.
